Made by scripts/validation-reports.py on 2026-10-23, femahoy 3493b3a.

This case checks the particle path: a 2D dam break with smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH). A water column falls on a dry floor, and the surge front moves along the floor. The reference is a measurement. Thus the tolerance comes from the scatter of the measurement and from the resolution study of the model.

Why this case

No other case of the suite has any of these items:

  • Particles: the solver is LAMMPS (SPH), not a mesh solver.
  • A free surface with a large motion.
  • Weakly compressible water: the Tait equation of state with an artificial speed of sound.
  • An explicit transient that stops when a quantity (the front position) gets to a value.

Source

J. C. Martin and W. J. Moyce, "Part IV. An experimental study of the collapse of liquid columns on a rigid horizontal plane", Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A 244 (1952) 312-324, https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1952.0006.

A column of water of width a and height n^2 a stands on a horizontal plane, against a wall at x = 0. At t = 0 the column is released. Table 2 (page 317) gives the times for n^2 = 2, a = 2.25 in, in the dimensionless form T = n t sqrt(g / a) = t sqrt(2 g / a) at the front positions Z = x / a. The source sets T to 1.19 at Z = 1.44 in each run ("T normalized at this value of Z"), because the instant of the release is not known exactly. The model does the same: it adds a constant to its T so that T is 1.19 at Z = 1.44.

The checks use the column "mean" for a = 2.25 in:

CheckZMeasured T (mean)Single runsStandard deviation of the runs
T_2112.111.839, from 1.75 to 1.880.048 (2.6 %)
T_3003.002.519, from 2.38 to 2.660.099 (3.9 %)
T_3893.893.114, from 2.94 to 3.250.139 (4.5 %)

The 3 points are near the start, the middle and the end of the data that the source gives for most runs of a = 2.25 in.

Model

The LAMMPS case is the folder sph: case.lmp. The units are SI.

ItemValue
Columna = 0.05715 m, height 2a, water from x = 0 to a
Particlesa square grid with spacing dx = a / 40 = 1.43 mm. 3200 water particles
Walls3 layers of fixed particles: the wall at x <= 0 to a height of 2.5a, and the floor at y <= 0 to x = 6a. Their density follows the continuity equation (fix sph/stationary)
Waterrho0 = 1000 kg/m^3. The Tait equation p = B ((rho / rho0)^7 - 1), B = c0^2 rho0 / 7, c0 = 20 m/s. c0 is more than 10 times the largest speed, sqrt(2 g 2a) = 1.5 m/s
Kernelthe Lucy kernel of LAMMPS, radius h = 3 dx
Viscositythe artificial viscosity of Monaghan, alpha = 0.05 (pair_style sph/taitwater)
Startat rest, with the hydrostatic density of the Tait equation
Time stepdt = 0.025 h / c0 = 5.4e-6 s
Frontthe largest x of the water plus dx / 2
Outputfront.txt: 1 row with the 3 values of the check. particles.dump: the water every 4000 steps, with the speed and the pressure, for the viewer

The run stops at each Z with fix halt. The last stop is at Z = 3.89, at t = 0.17 s. The water does not get to the end of the floor.

Problems that the model solves:

  • With dt = 0.1 h / c0 and alpha = 0.02, the density goes from 400 to 1350 kg/m^3 and particles leave the box. A smaller time step removes this.
  • With dt = 0.05 h / c0 and alpha = 0.02, T is 6 % to 21 % too small at n = 80, and 1 % to 18 % too large at n = 40. With dt = 0.025 h / c0, the values change little from n = 40 to n = 80.

Studies

These commands, in the repository root, solve the case with other values in a scratch folder. -var sets the variables n, alpha and cfl of case.lmp:

mkdir /tmp/dam && cp validation/cases/dam-break-martin-moyce/sph/case.lmp /tmp/dam && cd /tmp/dam
lmp -in case.lmp -log none -var n 80

The values are in /tmp/dam/front.txt.

Tolerance

The tolerance is rel_tol = 0.07 and abs_tol = 0.

CauseBasisEffect
The scatter of the measurementThe largest standard deviation of the single runs about the mean (at Z = 3.89, 4 runs)4.5 %
Resolution error of the modelThe extrapolation of T_389 from 3 resolutions2.4 %

rel_tol is the sum, 6.9 %, rounded up to 7 %. The front of the model is slower than the mean at all 3 points. The extrapolated values (1.864, 2.557, 3.169) are 1.9 % above the means, less than 1 standard deviation of the runs.

CheckModelMeasuredDifferenceTolerancePart of the tolerance
T_2111.8671.830.0370.12829 %
T_3002.5962.510.0860.17649 %
T_3893.2443.110.1340.21861 %

The tolerance stops these errors:

  • The coarse model (n = 20): T_300 and T_389 fail.
  • A time step that is too large (dt = 0.05 h / c0 with alpha = 0.02): T_300 is 18 % too large and fails.

Not in the check

  • The height of the column at x = 0, the second measurement of the source. It needs a second rule for the surface of the particles.
  • Z larger than 4.11: only 3 of the 9 runs of a = 2.25 in have data there, and the run takes longer.
  • The other column of the source, a = 1.125 in: it has the same n^2 and thus the same T(Z) in theory.

On a Mac with 10 cores, fh validate of the case took 24 s on 1 core with LAMMPS of 30 Sep 2026.
